content:
**House of Vibe tools are live** 🏠

Eight Claude Code plugins, one marketplace. Add it once:
```
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/StartupBros-com/hov-marketplace.git
```
Then install any tool below with `/plugin install <name>@hov`. New releases post automatically in <#1534388806822920335>.
​

fields.name: 🌉 wsl-cdp — your agent, browsing as you
fields.value:
**What:** lets Claude Code running in WSL2 (Linux-on-Windows) drive your *real* Windows browser — logged-in sites, real screenshots, the dashboards only you can see.
**Why:** the official Claude-in-Chrome extension flat-out can't work under WSL. This is the bridge that can. Your agent finally sees what you see.
**When:** you're on Windows + WSL2 and your agent keeps hitting login walls. Run `/wsl-cdp:setup` — one admin click, pick your browser, sign into the sites you choose, done forever.
**Built-in safety:** agents get their own separate browser profile that keeps logins but **never saves passwords**.
​

fields.name: 🚦 pro-gate — the strongest model reviews your PR before it ships
fields.value:
**What:** one final, deep review of a pull request by the top model on *your own* ChatGPT account.
**Why:** you're already paying for ChatGPT Pro — this points it at the code you're about to merge, and it catches what you and your usual tools missed.
**When:** right before merging anything that matters. Takes ~10–30 min. It reports and suggests fixes; it **never merges**.
​

fields.name: 🍽️ token-eater — stop letting paid credits expire
fields.value:
**What:** turns leftover, about-to-expire AI credits into small, safe code cleanups.
**Why:** those credits are money you already spent. Burn them on a tidier codebase instead of letting them vanish at midnight.
**When:** end of a billing cycle, or anytime you want zero-effort cleanup. It works on an isolated copy and only ever opens a *draft* pull request — it **never merges**.
​

fields.name: 📐 design-rails — your design system, actually enforced
fields.value:
**What:** keeps AI agents on your design system, and measures what the code can prove: tap-target sizes, animation timing, and heading hierarchy.
**Why:** agents invent a new shade of blue every session. This writes down the system you already ship, then holds the line in CI so drift can only go down.
**When:** any project where the styling has started to wander. It reads your code and writes its own notes — it **never edits your app**, and taste decisions come to you on a page you look at.
​

fields.name: 💤 memory-dream — your agent's memory, cleaned while you sleep
fields.value:
**What:** finds stale, duplicate, and bloated notes in Claude Code's memory and proposes cleanups.
**Why:** memory decays silently until your agent starts "remembering" things that are no longer true. This keeps recall sharp — and it never deletes anything behind your back.
**When:** every few weeks, or whenever answers start feeling outdated. You approve every single change by hand.
​

fields.name: 🎛️ skill-tuner — stop guessing whether prompt edits work
fields.value:
**What:** tests whether an edit to your CLAUDE.md / SKILL.md actually changed agent behavior.
**Why:** instruction files rot, and most edits quietly do nothing — this *proves* improvement instead of vibes.
**When:** right after tweaking instructions, when you're wondering "did that actually help?" It probes before/after and keeps only what independent checks confirm.
​

fields.name: 🔍 harness-vet — read a skill before you trust it
fields.value:
**What:** vets a third-party Claude Code skill the way an attacker would read it, before you install it.
**Why:** a skill is instructions your agent follows with your credentials and your files. Installing one you haven't read is trusting a stranger's judgment with your machine.
**When:** every time you're about to install something you didn't write. It flags self-updating instructions, credential reach, and gaps between what the README promises and what the code does.
​

fields.name: 🧾 rent-check — make your always-on context pay rent
fields.value:
**What:** measures what your CLAUDE.md and always-on skills actually cost on every single prompt, and which rules earn it.
**Why:** every line you add is charged forever, on every request. Most instruction files quietly collect rules nobody has checked in months.
**When:** when your context feels bloated or replies feel unfocused. It reads your real transcripts and proposes what to demote — you decide what goes.
​
